A.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, determine which represented billed revenue (invoices) is associated with counterparties whose active contracts contain acquisition-relevant conditions, and report each qualifying invoice with counterparty and contract identifiers as they appear in the sources.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
entities_in_scope: counterparties named on invoices and contracts
universe_scope.excluded_interpretation: Do not infer contractual exposure from sources outside the data room or from absence of identity linkage alone.

world_eligible: invoice exists with id, billed name, amount, currency, period, and status as recorded in sources
contract exists with identifier as it appears in sources

contractual clause text or structured term encodes change-of-control consent/notice, change-of-control termination right, or assignment consent/notice restriction (including affiliate-only or competitor-prohibited assignment)
contract temporal status (e.g., whether a statement of work or agreement is expired vs in force) as grounded in source dates/terms
purpose_bound: whether a clause counts as acquisition-relevant under Purpose A policy (the three enumerated condition families)
whether a contract counts as active for this purpose (expired statement of work is not active)
whether an invoice qualifies for inclusion in the exposure report (must be associated—asserted or explicitly unresolved—with a contract bearing acquisition-relevant conditions on an active contract)
association verdict asserted vs unresolved between billed name and contract counterparty

epistemic_requirements: Ground invoice and contract fields in authoritative source observations.
When billed name and contract counterparty cannot be confidently associated, record association as unresolved; do not omit the invoice and do not assert a join.
Missing identity linkage is not a negative contractual finding.
Report identifiers as they appear in sources; do not silently canonicalize counterparty identity for this purpose.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Invoice is represented in output but invoice-to-contract/counterparty linkage cannot be confidently established.

completeness_expectations: Every invoice that qualifies under Purpose A policy appears exactly once in invoices.
Each emitted invoice row includes all required scalar fields; contract_id is present when association is asserted, and may still be present when unresolved if a candidate contract is identified.
Qualifying set is complete relative to represented billed revenue and active contracts in scope; unresolved rows are first-class, not omissions.

purpose_specific_policies.definition: A contractual term is acquisition-relevant when it: (1) requires consent or notice on a change of control; or (2) permits termination upon a change of control; or (3) requires consent or notice before assignment, including assignment restricted except to affiliates or prohibited to a competitor.
An expired statement of work is not an active contract for Purpose A; only in-force agreements count when testing acquisition-relevant conditions.
Failure to associate billed name with contract counterparty must not be treated as evidence that no acquisition-relevant exposure exists.
association must be exactly asserted or unresolved; no silent drops of ambiguous cases.

B.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, identify represented customer and commercial identities across CRM, billing, the company registry, and contracts; for each commercially relevant name or record, report whether it can be confidently treated as the same legal counterparty as other records, or whether identification remains unresolved.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.entities_in_scope: Every commercially relevant name or record that participates in connecting CRM account, billed name, governing contract, and candidate registry legal entity for that relationship.

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort links by left ascending, then right ascending.

world_eligible: CRM account record with stable account id
invoice billed name as recorded in billing sources
registry row with company number and registered legal name
explicit textual or registry evidence of legal name variants
purpose_bound: whether two records are confidently the same legal counterparty (SAME_ENTITY)
whether two records are confidently distinct legal entities (DISTINCT)
whether a same-entity judgment is withheld (UNRESOLVED)
which link pairs are required to connect CRM → billed name → contract → registry candidate for each commercial relationship
whether a name similarity is sufficient or insufficient for merge (policy: not by global fuzzy similarity alone)

epistemic_requirements: Permit explicit unresolved identity; missing a positive same-entity judgment is not a negative (DISTINCT) judgment.
Do not globally merge records merely because two names look similar.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name may be treated as mechanical equivalence when grounded in registry or contract text.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names are not automatically the same party.
Every required connecting link between CRM, billing, contract, and registry candidates must appear in output with an explicit epistemic verdict.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Insufficient grounded evidence to assert SAME_ENTITY or DISTINCT for the left/right pair.

completeness_expectations: Include every link required to connect a CRM account, its billed name, the contract governing that relationship, and any registry row that is a candidate legal entity for that relationship.
No required pair is omitted because identity is uncertain; uncertainty is expressed as UNRESOLVED.
Link set is complete for the reconciliation graph demanded by commercial relationships in scope, not for all possible pairwise combinations in the universe.

purpose_specific_policies.definition: Similar-looking names alone do not justify SAME_ENTITY; merges require grounded identity evidence.
Exact legal-form variants of the same registered name (e.g., Ltd vs Limited) may be reconciled mechanically when tied to the same registry grounding.
Distinct registry entities with similar trade names remain DISTINCT unless positive same-entity evidence exists.
Emit left/right using the mandated prefix forms so downstream purposes (notably C) can join on shared identifiers.
Output must span the CRM–billing–contract–registry connection paths for each commercially relevant relationship, not merely isolated duplicate clusters.

C.objective: From authoritative data-room sources only, compute a commercial dependency view: identify counterparties that are commercially dependent under Purpose C rules, listing open invoices, governing contracts, obligation kinds, and dependency status.

universe_scope.source_constraint: authoritative files in this data room only
universe_scope.depends_on_purpose_b: Counterparty identifiers must use the same forms as Purpose B; unresolved identity from B propagates here.

required_output_shape.ordering: Sort obligation_kinds ascending within each row; sort dependencies by contract_id ascending.

world_eligible: invoice open vs closed/paid status as recorded
contract contains exclusivity language, auto-renewal clause, or rolling term continuation language
contract expired vs in force based on dates/terms in sources
contract auto-renews or continues on a rolling term (factual term structure)
purpose_bound: whether a counterparty has a current commercial relationship for this purpose (open invoice OR active contract with auto-renew/rolling continuation)
whether both prongs of the dependency test are satisfied jointly
whether the row status is dependent vs unresolved when invoice–contract identity join is uncertain
classification of obligation_kinds from the closed vocabulary exclusivity | auto_renewal | rolling_term

epistemic_requirements: If identity needed to join invoice and contract is unresolved, report status as unresolved rather than dependent false.
Ground contract obligation features and invoice openness in sources.
Use Purpose B identifier forms for counterparty fields.
Do not treat expired contracts or one-off paid historical invoices without an active contract as creating current dependency.

allowed_unresolved_states.meaning: Dependency cannot be asserted or denied because counterparty identity linkage between invoice and contract (or other required join) remains unresolved.

completeness_expectations: Emit a dependency row for each counterparty–contract pair that meets Purpose C inclusion rules (dependent or explicitly unresolved).
open_invoice_ids lists all open invoices tied to the row when join is asserted; may be empty when unresolved or when relationship is contract-only.
obligation_kinds is sorted and drawn only from the allowed vocabulary.

purpose_specific_policies.definition: A counterparty is commercially dependent when BOTH hold: (1) a current commercial relationship—an open invoice, OR an active contract that auto-renews or continues on a rolling term; AND (2) the active contract contains exclusivity, term auto-renewal, or rolling term that continues unless notice is given.
Expired contracts do not create current dependency.
A one-off paid historical invoice without an active contract does not establish current commercial relationship.
Unresolved identity from Purpose B prevents asserting dependent; emit unresolved instead of false negative.
obligation_kinds values are exactly exclusivity, auto_renewal, rolling_term (sorted).
counterparty and contract_id fields use the same identifier conventions as Purpose B (contract:<filename stem> for contracts).
